description: ns-3 is a discrete-event network simulator for research and education, the most widely used open-source tool for simulating packet networks. It contains protocol and channel models for the Internet stack (IPv4, IPv6, TCP, routing), Wi-Fi, LTE and other cellular technologies, point-to-point and CSMA links, mobility models and energy models; release 3.48 (June 2026) added mobility support for low-earth-orbit satellite constellations, 6LoWPAN neighbour discovery and a Sionna RT ray-traced channel model. A real-time scheduler lets ns-3 run as a network emulator connected to real hosts, and real application and kernel code can be reused. It is produced by an open-source community coordinated by the ns-3 Consortium, with a new stable release about every three months and a companion ns-allinone bundle of about fifteen contributed extension modules. Coverage: generic, technology-level models with no geographic limitation. Format and access: C++ source with Python bindings, built with CMake on Linux and macOS, downloaded from the website or the GitLab repository; it is free of charge under the GNU GPLv2 licence. Caveats: simulations are packet-level and scale poorly to whole national networks without abstraction; model fidelity varies by module; there is no GUI apart from the NetAnim animator. Simulation uses: network flow and capacity planning of access and backbone networks, resilience and cascading-failure studies of communication networks, and co-simulation of communication with power or transport systems as part of a digital twin. Related records: OMNeT++, Mininet and Sionna are alternative or complementary tools; SNDlib and CAIDA topologies can supply network inputs.
